One of the objectives for the TES was to allow discrimination of smoke
constituent exposure from cigarettes that differ by
1 mg of FTC "tar". The population size for the TES was to be defined based
on this objective. Assuming for simplicity that 1 mg "tar" is equivalent to 0.1
mg nicotine, what population size would you calculate for the TES study from
the data provided in Table 3 of the latest Jarvis study ?
M.J. Jarvis, R. Boreham, P. Primatesta, C. Feyerabend, and A. Bryant (2000).
Nicotine yield from machine-smoked cigarettes and nicotine intakes in
smokers: evidence from a population survey. Journal of the National Cancer
